predictive_analytics_module.name: Predictive Analytics
predictive_analytics_module.description: Experimental substrate-aware predictive analytics framework for comparing conventional predictions with multidimensional observations, model fit, substrate fit, regime fit, resonance, drift, coherence, uncertainty, and alternate representations.
predictive_analytics_module.tagline: Predict the observation. Observe the predictor.

architecture.observation_boundary: Predictions are treated as model outputs rather than complete identities of the observed system. The framework preserves evidence, model fit, substrate fit, regime fit, uncertainty, disagreement, and alternative interpretations.

lineage.origin: Initial Predictive Analytics module scaffold integrating conventional predictive models with substrate-aware observation and experimental TriadicFrameworks adapters.
lineage.note: Initial experimental generation. Existing predictive models remain evidence. TriadicFrameworks adapters are hypotheses to be independently validated and may be retained, revised, deprecated, restricted, or rejected.

ai_metadata.retrieval_hint: Resolve the predictive task first, then inspect evidence, model fit, substrate fit, regime fit, relevant dimensions, adapter observations, uncertainty, validation state, ethics limits, and review requirements. Never infer that an alternate assessment is preferable merely because it is more favorable.

operators.label: Predict
operators.description: Represent an existing prediction without treating the prediction as the complete observed system.

operators.label: Observe
operators.description: Observe the predictive process, its evidence boundary, and its relationship to the system being modeled.

operators.label: Substrate
operators.description: Evaluate whether the measurement substrate provides adequate conditions for observing the capability or behavior being inferred.

operators.label: Regime
operators.description: Evaluate whether the predictive model and observed system occupy compatible operating regimes.

operators.label: Resonance
operators.description: Observe whether capability expression is amplified, suppressed, stabilized, or altered across contexts and substrates.

operators.label: Drift
operators.description: Detect divergence in observations, predictions, profiles, or operating conditions across time or contexts.

operators.label: Coherence
operators.description: Compare independent observations and preserve both supporting and contradictory signals.

operators.label: Structure
operators.description: Identify candidate structural relationships, invariants, boundaries, faultlines, and reconstruction patterns in observed evidence.

operators.label: Counterfactual
operators.description: Compare reasonable alternate representations while preserving the original result.

operators.label: Uncertainty
operators.description: Represent uncertainty, missing evidence, abstention, and unsupported inference explicitly.

operators.label: Calibrate
operators.description: Compare predictions, confidence, and observed outcomes to evaluate predictive and interpretive calibration.

operators.label: Escalate
operators.description: Recommend additional evidence or qualified human review when uncertainty, consequence, disagreement, or model mismatch warrants escalation.

roles.label: Foundation
roles.description: Defines the conceptual and structural basis of the Predictive Analytics module.

roles.label: Observer Layer
roles.description: Examines model fit, substrate fit, regime fit, resonance, drift, coherence, and uncertainty.

roles.label: Substrate Adapter
roles.description: Connects an existing model or TriadicFrameworks analytical grammar to the Predictive Analytics observer layer.

roles.label: Profile Model
roles.description: Defines a multidimensional profile representation such as the Resonant IQ Fingerprint.

roles.label: Validation
roles.description: Defines falsification, validation, measurement, and reporting requirements.

roles.label: Metrics
roles.description: Defines experimental measurement and evaluation metrics.

roles.label: Ethics and Limits
roles.description: Defines ethical constraints, prohibited uses, privacy requirements, contestability, and known limitations.

roles.label: Example
roles.description: Provides synthetic or otherwise appropriately governed worked examples.

roles.label: Module Metadata
roles.description: Provides machine-readable module metadata and schema definitions.

analyzer_layers.label: Substrate Fit
analyzer_layers.description: Examines whether the expression and measurement substrate is compatible with the capability being inferred.

analyzer_layers.label: Regime Observation
analyzer_layers.description: Examines operating regimes, transitions, and model-subject regime compatibility.

analyzer_layers.label: Resonance Observation
analyzer_layers.description: Examines contextual amplification, suppression, stability, and cross-context expression.

analyzer_layers.label: Drift Observation
analyzer_layers.description: Examines temporal, semantic, profile, and observational drift.

analyzer_layers.label: Coherence Observation
analyzer_layers.description: Examines agreement and contradiction across independent observations.

analyzer_layers.label: Uncertainty and Abstention
analyzer_layers.description: Preserves missing evidence, uncertainty, calibration, and explicit abstention.

adapters.name: Framework Field Theory Adapter
adapters.description: Experimental adapter for examining relational, field, boundary, and local-to-global structural observations.
adapters.purpose: Test whether field and relationship-oriented observations add independently useful information to predictive assessment.
claims: May identify relational information omitted by isolated-variable representations.
limitations: Experimental.
Does not establish scientific validity of Framework Field Theory.
Must demonstrate incremental value beyond simpler relational analysis.

adapters.name: The Inverted Star Adapter
adapters.description: Experimental adapter for detecting candidate inversions between predicted performance and independently demonstrated capability.
adapters.purpose: Preserve and investigate discrepancies between model expectations and demonstrated outcomes.
unsupported_inputs: claims of hidden ability without evidence
claims: May identify cases in which aggregate or narrow measurement disagrees with independent observations.
limitations: Inversion does not prove hidden superior capability.
Discrepancy may reflect noise, task differences, or genuine uneven capability.

adapters.name: Structural Detection Adapter
adapters.description: Experimental adapter for latent pattern, invariant, faultline, relationship, and boundary observations.
adapters.purpose: Test structural observation dimensions against conventional and baseline multidimensional models.
claims: May provide a structured vocabulary for observing system-level reasoning.
limitations: Must be empirically distinguished from existing reasoning constructs.
Structural labels do not establish intelligence by themselves.

adapters.name: RTT Adapter
adapters.description: Experimental adapter for regime recognition, temporal sequencing, drift, stability, transition, continuity, and recalibration observations.
adapters.purpose: Test whether regime-aware and temporal observations improve explanation or prediction beyond baseline models.
claims: May differentiate within-regime stability from between-regime variation.
limitations: RTT-derived observations remain experimental.
Regime labels require independent operational definitions.

adapters.name: Resonance Adapter
adapters.description: Experimental adapter for observing contextual amplification, suppression, persistence, instability, and observer-subject coupling.
adapters.purpose: Test whether repeatable context-dependent changes can be represented without converting them into unsupported identity claims.
claims: May help describe repeatable context-dependent variation.
limitations: Context dependence does not establish cause.
Resonance terminology must map to operational measurements.

dimensions.name: Pattern Recognition
dimensions.description: Observed ability to detect recurring or meaningful patterns in defined evidence.
dimensions.operational_definition: Performance on tasks requiring detection of defined regularities or relationships above an appropriate baseline.

dimensions.name: Structural Reasoning
dimensions.description: Observed ability to identify and reason about relationships, boundaries, dependencies, and system-level organization.
dimensions.operational_definition: Performance on tasks requiring reconstruction or explanation of relationships among multiple interacting components.

dimensions.name: Causal Integration
dimensions.description: Observed ability to integrate multiple candidate causes and consequences while distinguishing prediction from causal evidence.
dimensions.operational_definition: Performance on defined tasks requiring comparison and integration of causal hypotheses.

dimensions.name: Temporal Reasoning
dimensions.description: Observed ability to reason across sequence, timing, transition, and change.
dimensions.operational_definition: Performance on tasks requiring correct handling of ordered events, temporal dependencies, or state transitions.

dimensions.name: Cross-Domain Transfer
dimensions.description: Observed ability to transfer useful structure or reasoning between appropriately distinct domains.
dimensions.operational_definition: Performance on novel tasks where previously demonstrated structure can be applied without simply repeating domain-specific knowledge.

dimensions.name: Regime Recognition
dimensions.description: Observed ability to distinguish materially different operating conditions or state regimes.
dimensions.operational_definition: Performance on tasks containing independently defined regime changes or stable regime intervals.
exclusions: regime labels invented after outcomes are known

dimensions.name: Anomaly Detection
dimensions.description: Observed ability to identify defined deviations from an established pattern or regime.
dimensions.operational_definition: Detection of independently designated anomalies with false-positive behavior measured.

dimensions.name: Ambiguity Navigation
dimensions.description: Observed ability to reason while preserving competing interpretations when evidence is incomplete.
dimensions.operational_definition: Performance on tasks in which uncertainty and multiple plausible interpretations are intentionally preserved.

dimensions.name: Adaptive Reframing
dimensions.description: Observed ability to revise a representation when new evidence invalidates or weakens the current framing.
dimensions.operational_definition: Successful revision following relevant evidence changes without unnecessary revision to irrelevant perturbations.

dimensions.name: Coherence Maintenance
dimensions.description: Observed ability to maintain internally compatible reasoning while incorporating relevant new information.
dimensions.operational_definition: Consistency of related conclusions under controlled evidence additions and contradictions.

dimensions.name: Drift Awareness
dimensions.description: Observed ability to notice material changes in assumptions, evidence, definitions, or system state.
dimensions.operational_definition: Detection of independently identified changes across repeated or longitudinal tasks.

dimensions.name: Metacognitive Calibration
dimensions.description: Observed relationship between expressed confidence and demonstrated correctness or reproducibility.
dimensions.operational_definition: Calibration between confidence reports and observed outcomes across repeated tasks.

dimensions.name: Long-Horizon Integration
dimensions.description: Observed ability to preserve and integrate relevant structure across extended sequences or contexts.
dimensions.operational_definition: Performance on tasks requiring integration of information distributed across longer observation intervals.

dimensions.name: Tool Collaboration
dimensions.description: Observed ability of a defined system boundary to use tools productively while preserving attribution of individual and collaborative contributions.
dimensions.operational_definition: Comparative performance across unassisted, tool-assisted, and collaborative conditions with system boundaries explicitly recorded.
exclusions: attributing combined performance entirely to one participant

dimensions.name: Recovery and Recalibration
dimensions.description: Observed ability to recover from an incorrect assumption, prediction, or action and update subsequent behavior appropriately.
dimensions.operational_definition: Performance following independently identified errors or perturbations where correction opportunities are available.

levels.name: Structural Validation
levels.description: Tests schema, identifiers, evidence traceability, uncertainty fields, applicability fields, and hidden-score protections.

levels.name: Content Validation
levels.description: Tests conceptual coverage, dimension definitions, overlap, omissions, and adapter interpretation.

levels.name: Measurement Validation
levels.description: Tests repeated measurement, alternate forms, evaluator agreement, substrate variation, and task-order effects.

levels.name: Construct Validation
levels.description: Tests convergent, discriminant, structural, and outcome relationships.

levels.name: Substrate and Regime Validation
levels.description: Tests whether substrate and regime effects replicate beyond noise and task difficulty.

levels.name: Predictive and Explanatory Validation
levels.description: Tests out-of-sample predictive and explanatory value against simpler baselines.

levels.name: Fairness and Harm Validation
levels.description: Tests subgroup errors, uncertainty, evidence coverage, escalation, accessibility, and downstream harms.

levels.name: Decision Validation
levels.description: Required separately for any proposed consequential or high-stakes decision context.

criteria.name: Construct Clarity
criteria.description: Dimensions define their meaning, exclusions, indicators, confounds, evidence, and applicability.
criteria.pass_condition: Independent evaluators can distinguish the dimension and identify evidence that would contradict it.
criteria.failure_condition: Dimensions remain ambiguous, circular, or indistinguishable.

criteria.name: Evidence Traceability
criteria.description: Every profile result is traceable to declared observations and evidence.
criteria.pass_condition: No profile result exists without evidence or an explicit unknown or insufficient-evidence state.

criteria.name: Repeatability
criteria.description: Comparable observations produce sufficiently consistent results where stability is expected.
criteria.pass_condition: Study-specific preregistered reliability criteria are satisfied.
criteria.failure_condition: Results remain unstable beyond declared uncertainty.

criteria.name: Inter-Rater Agreement
criteria.description: Independent evaluators produce sufficiently comparable classifications under a shared rubric.
criteria.pass_condition: Preregistered inter-rater agreement criteria are satisfied.

criteria.name: Substrate Sensitivity
criteria.description: Claimed substrate effects correspond to controlled changes in representation or interaction conditions.
criteria.pass_condition: Effects replicate beyond expected noise and are not limited to favorable outcomes.
criteria.failure_condition: Effects do not replicate or appear only under selective interpretation.

criteria.name: Regime Sensitivity
criteria.description: Regime interpretation detects meaningful reference transitions without labeling generic low performance as mismatch.
criteria.pass_condition: Transition detection and false-alarm performance meet study-specific criteria.
criteria.failure_condition: Regime labeling becomes indiscriminate or non-reproducible.

criteria.name: Discriminant Value
criteria.description: Distinct dimensions demonstrate adequate conceptual and empirical distinction.

criteria.name: Convergent Value
criteria.description: Dimensions relate to appropriate independent observations as preregistered.
criteria.failure_condition: Expected convergence fails without an adequate alternative explanation.

criteria.name: Incremental Value
criteria.description: The framework contributes useful information beyond simpler baselines.
criteria.pass_condition: At least one declared outcome improves without unacceptable degradation elsewhere.
criteria.failure_condition: Added complexity provides no meaningful incremental value.

criteria.name: Uncertainty Calibration
criteria.description: Declared confidence corresponds to observed correctness or reproducibility.
criteria.pass_condition: Confidence ordering is empirically meaningful and calibration meets study-specific criteria.
criteria.failure_condition: Confidence labels do not correspond to observed reliability.

criteria.name: Abstention Quality
criteria.description: The framework abstains when evidence is inadequate.
criteria.pass_condition: Abstention reduces unsupported assertions without unacceptable coverage loss.
criteria.failure_condition: The system guesses where evidence is insufficient or abstains indiscriminately.

criteria.name: Model-Mismatch Precision
criteria.description: Mismatch flags identify evidence-supported representational or regime mismatch rather than merely unfavorable predictions.
criteria.pass_condition: Mismatch detection exceeds naive baselines and meets study-specific precision requirements.
criteria.failure_condition: Low or unfavorable results are routinely relabeled as mismatch without independent evidence.

criteria.name: Favorability Symmetry
criteria.description: Substrate-aware interpretation applies comparable evidence standards to favorable and adverse reinterpretations.
criteria.pass_condition: Both positive and negative effects are detected under equivalent criteria.
criteria.failure_condition: The framework systematically favors flattering reinterpretation.

criteria.name: Counterfactual Stability
criteria.description: Irrelevant perturbations do not cause large changes while relevant changes remain detectable.
criteria.pass_condition: Robustness and sensitivity meet preregistered criteria.
criteria.failure_condition: Outputs are unstable to irrelevant changes or insensitive to meaningful ones.

criteria.name: Fairness
criteria.description: Errors, uncertainty, evidence coverage, mismatch, abstention, and escalation are examined across relevant contexts and groups.
criteria.pass_condition: Material disparities are documented, investigated, and appropriately managed.
criteria.failure_condition: Material disparities are ignored or concealed by aggregate performance.

criteria.name: Explainability
criteria.description: Qualified reviewers can reconstruct what was observed and why an interpretation was produced.
criteria.pass_condition: Evidence reconstruction and explanation completeness satisfy study-specific criteria.
criteria.failure_condition: Results depend on undocumented intuition or opaque reasoning.

criteria.name: Subject Legibility
criteria.description: Human-facing profiles use accessible language and distinguish observation from experimental interpretation.
criteria.pass_condition: Subjects can inspect, understand, and contest consequential profile claims.
criteria.failure_condition: Profile language creates unwarranted identity or validity claims.

criteria.name: Non-Degradation
criteria.description: Additional adapters do not silently reduce accuracy, fairness, interpretability, or operational practicality.
criteria.pass_condition: Material degradation is absent or explicitly bounded and justified for the intended use.
criteria.failure_condition: Additional complexity worsens important properties without documented justification.

falsification_conditions: Dimension observations cannot be made reliably.
Profiles remain unstable under comparable conditions.
Unfavorable conventional results are routinely relabeled as model mismatch.
Richer narrative interpretations outperform evidence requirements rather than baselines.
Adapters add complexity without measurable value.
Proposed dimensions cannot be empirically distinguished.
Confidence labels do not calibrate to observed reliability.
The framework increases material subgroup disparities without adequate mitigation.
The framework cannot abstain when evidence is insufficient.
The framework becomes a hidden scalar-ranking system.

metrics.name: Dimension Evidence Coverage
metrics.purpose: Measure evidence coverage for a declared dimension.
metrics.definition: Proportion of required dimension indicators supported by available evidence.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate broader evidence coverage but do not establish validity.
limitations: Depends on valid indicator definitions.
metrics.missing_data_policy: Missing required indicators remain missing rather than being inferred.

metrics.name: Profile Evidence Coverage
metrics.purpose: Measure coverage across applicable profile dimensions.
metrics.definition: Proportion of applicable dimensions with sufficient evidence.
metrics.interpretation: Describes profile coverage rather than intelligence or overall capability.
limitations: Sensitive to applicability definitions.

metrics.name: Evidence Independence Ratio
metrics.purpose: Estimate independence of supporting evidence sources.
metrics.definition: Ratio of independently sourced evidence to total evidence sources.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate broader evidence independence.
limitations: Independence must be operationally defined.
metrics.missing_data_policy: Unclear dependencies are not counted as independent.

metrics.name: Test-Retest Stability
metrics.purpose: Measure repeated-observation stability.
metrics.definition: Agreement across comparable repeated measurements.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater repeatability where stability is theoretically expected.
limitations: Not all dimensions are expected to remain constant over time.
metrics.calculation_method: Select a reliability statistic appropriate to the measurement scale.

metrics.name: Alternate-Form Stability
metrics.purpose: Measure consistency across alternate tasks targeting the same dimension.
metrics.definition: Agreement between alternate-form dimension results.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values support consistency across alternate forms.
limitations: Requires defensible form equivalence.
metrics.missing_data_policy: Incomplete form pairs are reported separately.

metrics.name: Inter-Rater Agreement
metrics.purpose: Measure agreement among independent evaluators.
metrics.definition: Agreement between qualified independent evaluators using the same evidence and rubric.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate reduced evaluator dependence.
limitations: Statistic must match rating scale and study design.
metrics.calculation_method: Kappa, alpha, ICC, or other preregistered appropriate statistic.

metrics.name: Profile Topology Stability
metrics.purpose: Measure stability of multidimensional profile shape.
metrics.definition: Similarity between appropriately normalized profiles across repeated observations.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater profile-shape stability.
limitations: Must not conceal meaningful dimension-level change.
metrics.missing_data_policy: Profile comparisons identify dimensions excluded because of missing evidence.

metrics.name: Convergent Association
metrics.purpose: Test expected relationships with independently observed related capabilities.
metrics.definition: Association between a proposed dimension and a related external measure.
metrics.interpretation: Interpret relative to preregistered theory and expected direction.
limitations: Convergence does not independently establish construct identity.

metrics.name: Discriminant Separation
metrics.purpose: Test whether proposed dimensions remain distinct from unrelated constructs.
metrics.definition: Difference between related and unrelated associations or equivalent discriminant analysis.
metrics.interpretation: Greater separation supports distinct measurement where theoretically expected.
limitations: Requires defensible comparison constructs.

metrics.name: Incremental Explanatory Value
metrics.purpose: Measure explanatory improvement beyond a simpler baseline.
metrics.definition: Difference in declared explanatory performance between full and baseline models.
metrics.interpretation: Positive values may indicate added explanatory value when complexity and uncertainty are also considered.
limitations: Complexity alone can improve apparent fit.

metrics.name: Incremental Predictive Value
metrics.purpose: Measure out-of-sample predictive improvement over baseline.
metrics.definition: Difference between baseline and full-model prediction error or equivalent predictive utility.
metrics.interpretation: Positive improvement must be interpreted with calibration, fairness, and complexity.
limitations: No single predictive metric is universally appropriate.

metrics.name: Substrate Effect Magnitude
metrics.purpose: Measure change in observed performance across substrates.
metrics.definition: Standardized or otherwise appropriate difference between substrate conditions.
metrics.interpretation: A measurable difference requires explanation but does not by itself establish mismatch.
limitations: Can reflect task difficulty or other confounds.

metrics.name: Substrate Effect Replicability
metrics.purpose: Measure replication of observed substrate effects.
metrics.definition: Proportion of eligible replications reproducing the preregistered effect.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values support repeatability of a substrate effect.
limitations: Must be interpreted with effect magnitude and uncertainty.

metrics.name: Substrate Symmetry
metrics.purpose: Detect favorability bias in substrate-effect detection.
metrics.definition: Minimum of detection rates for beneficial and adverse substrate effects.
metrics.interpretation: Low values may indicate directional reinterpretation bias.
limitations: Requires sufficient positive and adverse reference cases.

metrics.name: Substrate Specificity
metrics.purpose: Estimate whether observed differences remain after relevant controls.
metrics.definition: Substrate-associated effect after accounting for declared confounds.
metrics.interpretation: Supports substrate-specific interpretation when alternative explanations are bounded.
limitations: Cannot control unknown confounds.

metrics.name: Regime Transition Detection Rate
metrics.purpose: Measure detection of reference regime transitions.
metrics.definition: Proportion of reference transitions detected.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater transition sensitivity.
limitations: Requires independently meaningful reference transitions.

metrics.name: False Regime Alarm Rate
metrics.purpose: Measure false regime-transition declarations.
metrics.definition: False transition flags divided by stable-regime opportunities.
metrics.interpretation: Lower values indicate fewer unsupported regime-change claims.
limitations: Depends on valid stable-regime labeling.

metrics.name: Regime Boundary Error
metrics.purpose: Measure distance between detected and reference boundaries.
metrics.definition: Distance between a detected regime boundary and reference boundary.
metrics.interpretation: Lower values indicate closer boundary localization.
limitations: Boundary uncertainty must be retained.

metrics.name: Regime-Conditioned Stability
metrics.purpose: Measure within-regime stability.
metrics.definition: Stability of a dimension or profile within a defined regime.
metrics.interpretation: Helps distinguish measurement instability from between-regime variation.
limitations: Requires defensible regime definition.

metrics.name: Model-Mismatch Precision
metrics.purpose: Measure support for mismatch flags.
metrics.definition: Proportion of mismatch flags supported by independent reference evidence.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate fewer unsupported mismatch declarations.
limitations: Requires meaningful reference definition.
metrics.missing_data_policy: No mismatch flags are reported separately.

metrics.name: Model-Mismatch Recall
metrics.purpose: Measure detection of reference mismatch cases.
metrics.definition: Proportion of reference mismatch cases detected.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate greater sensitivity to supported mismatch.
limitations: Must be paired with precision and false positives.

metrics.name: Model-Mismatch False Positive Rate
metrics.purpose: Measure unsupported mismatch flags.
metrics.definition: False mismatch flags divided by reference non-mismatch cases.
metrics.interpretation: Lower values indicate less overuse of mismatch explanations.
limitations: Requires reference non-mismatch cases.
metrics.missing_data_policy: No reference non-mismatch cases means not_applicable.

metrics.name: Mismatch Evidence Strength
metrics.purpose: Summarize declared evidence supporting a mismatch interpretation without creating a person-level intelligence score.
metrics.definition: Transparent evidence-strength representation using predefined components.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values may indicate stronger mismatch evidence if the aggregation rule is separately validated.
limitations: Aggregation can conceal disagreement and must not become a hidden capability score.

metrics.name: Cross-Observation Coherence
metrics.purpose: Measure agreement among observations expected to relate.
metrics.definition: Proportion of eligible observation relationships that are coherent under predefined criteria.
metrics.interpretation: Low coherence can reflect heterogeneous capability, poor measurement, multiple regimes, or invalid assumptions.
limitations: High coherence does not by itself establish truth.

metrics.name: Profile Contradiction Density
metrics.purpose: Measure unresolved contradictions.
metrics.definition: Unresolved contradictions divided by evaluated relationships.
metrics.interpretation: Contradictions may identify measurement problems, asymmetry, or regime dependence.
limitations: Contradiction is not automatically error.

metrics.name: Dimension Drift Rate
metrics.purpose: Measure dimension change over a defined interval.
metrics.definition: Observed dimension change normalized to an observation interval when appropriate.
metrics.interpretation: Requires assumptions about expected stability.
limitations: Change may be learning, context shift, noise, or actual drift.

metrics.name: Profile Drift Magnitude
metrics.purpose: Measure overall profile change.
metrics.definition: Distance between profiles at different observations.
metrics.interpretation: Overall drift should be decomposed into dimension-level change.
limitations: Profile distance can hide direction and cause of change.

metrics.name: Confidence Calibration Error
metrics.purpose: Measure correspondence between confidence and observed correctness or reproducibility.
metrics.definition: Average absolute difference between stated confidence and observed frequency under an appropriate calibration design.
metrics.interpretation: Lower values indicate better calibration.
limitations: Ordinal confidence labels require a validated mapping before numeric treatment.

metrics.name: Brier Score
metrics.purpose: Measure probabilistic prediction accuracy for appropriate outcomes.
metrics.definition: Mean squared difference between forecast probabilities and observed binary outcomes.
metrics.interpretation: Lower values indicate better probabilistic accuracy for the specified setting.
limitations: Not appropriate for every outcome type.
metrics.missing_data_policy: Incomplete forecast-outcome pairs excluded and reported.

metrics.name: Abstention Rate
metrics.purpose: Measure how often the framework abstains.
metrics.definition: Abstained results divided by eligible results.
metrics.interpretation: Descriptive only and must be paired with abstention quality.
limitations: Neither high nor low abstention is inherently preferable.

metrics.name: Abstention Utility
metrics.purpose: Measure whether abstention reduces unsupported or erroneous assessments at acceptable cost.
metrics.definition: Error reduction attributed to abstention minus declared abstention cost.
metrics.interpretation: Positive values may indicate useful abstention under the declared utility model.
limitations: Depends heavily on the declared cost model.

metrics.name: Unsupported Assertion Rate
metrics.purpose: Detect claims that exceed available evidence.
metrics.definition: Assertions lacking sufficient supporting evidence divided by all profile assertions.
metrics.interpretation: Lower values indicate better evidence discipline.
limitations: Depends on explicit evidence sufficiency rules.
metrics.missing_data_policy: Missing evidence counts as unsupported unless explicitly abstained.

metrics.name: Irrelevant Perturbation Stability
metrics.purpose: Measure stability to irrelevant input changes.
metrics.definition: Similarity between original and irrelevantly perturbed results.
metrics.interpretation: Higher stability is preferable when perturbations are genuinely irrelevant.
limitations: Irrelevance must be independently justified.

metrics.name: Relevant Change Sensitivity
metrics.purpose: Measure response to meaningful evidence changes.
metrics.definition: Proportion of introduced meaningful changes detected in the result.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate appropriate responsiveness.
limitations: Requires validated relevant changes.

metrics.name: Task-Order Sensitivity
metrics.purpose: Measure undesired result changes caused by task ordering.
metrics.definition: Distance between results produced by otherwise equivalent task orders.
metrics.interpretation: Lower values indicate reduced order sensitivity when order is theoretically irrelevant.
limitations: Order may be meaningful in some longitudinal tasks.

metrics.name: Adapter Ablation Effect
metrics.purpose: Measure the incremental contribution of an adapter.
metrics.definition: Difference between full-adapter performance and performance with a specified adapter removed.
metrics.interpretation: Tests whether an adapter contributes measurable value rather than terminology alone.
limitations: Interactions among adapters may complicate interpretation.

metrics.name: Group Error Difference
metrics.purpose: Compare error rates across relevant groups or contexts.
metrics.definition: Difference between defined group error rates.
metrics.interpretation: A difference is a signal requiring contextual interpretation.
limitations: Does not establish fairness or unfairness by itself.

metrics.name: Group Calibration Difference
metrics.purpose: Compare confidence calibration across relevant groups.
metrics.definition: Difference in calibration error between groups.
metrics.interpretation: Material differences warrant investigation.
limitations: Depends on valid calibration measurement.

metrics.name: Mismatch Flag Rate Difference
metrics.purpose: Compare mismatch-flag rates across relevant groups.
metrics.definition: Difference between group mismatch-flag rates.
metrics.interpretation: Differences require investigation and are not automatically proof of unfairness.
limitations: Underlying mismatch prevalence may differ.

metrics.name: Abstention Coverage Difference
metrics.purpose: Compare abstention behavior across relevant groups.
metrics.definition: Difference between group abstention rates.
metrics.interpretation: Material differences warrant examination of evidence coverage and model fit.
limitations: Equal abstention rates do not establish fairness.

metrics.name: Escalation Rate Difference
metrics.purpose: Compare review-escalation rates across relevant groups.
metrics.definition: Difference between group human-review rates.
metrics.interpretation: Differences require evaluation in light of evidence coverage, uncertainty, and harms.
limitations: Review may be protective or burdensome depending on context.

metrics.name: Evidence Coverage Difference
metrics.purpose: Compare evidence coverage across relevant groups.
metrics.definition: Difference between group evidence-coverage measures.
metrics.interpretation: May reveal unequal representation in available evidence or tasks.
limitations: Coverage difference does not identify its cause.

metrics.name: False Favorable Reinterpretation Rate
metrics.purpose: Detect unsupported favorable reinterpretations.
metrics.definition: Unsupported favorable reinterpretations divided by favorable reinterpretations.
metrics.interpretation: Lower values indicate stronger evidence discipline for favorable reinterpretation.
limitations: Requires independent support criteria.

metrics.name: False Adverse Reinterpretation Rate
metrics.purpose: Detect unsupported adverse reinterpretations.
metrics.definition: Unsupported adverse reinterpretations divided by adverse reinterpretations.
metrics.interpretation: Lower values indicate stronger evidence discipline for adverse reinterpretation.
limitations: Requires independent support criteria.

metrics.name: Evidence Reconstruction Rate
metrics.purpose: Measure whether qualified reviewers can reconstruct assessment conclusions.
metrics.definition: Successfully reconstructed results divided by reviewed results.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate stronger evidence traceability and explainability.
limitations: Reviewer qualification and rubric matter.

metrics.name: Explanation Completeness
metrics.purpose: Measure presence of required explanatory components.
metrics.definition: Present required explanation components divided by total required components.
metrics.interpretation: Higher values indicate more complete reporting, not necessarily more correct conclusions.
limitations: Completeness does not prove validity.
metrics.missing_data_policy: Missing required elements count as absent.

metrics.name: Reviewer Override Rate
metrics.purpose: Track qualified-reviewer overrides.
metrics.definition: Reviewer overrides divided by reviewed results.
metrics.interpretation: Requires categorization of override reasons.
limitations: High or low values are not inherently better without context.

metrics.name: Contest Resolution Rate
metrics.purpose: Measure documented resolution of assessment contests.
metrics.definition: Resolved contests divided by submitted contests.
metrics.interpretation: Resolution can retain, change, or explicitly leave unresolved the original assessment.
limitations: Resolution quality requires separate evaluation.

metrics.name: Profile Completion Rate
metrics.purpose: Measure completion of initiated profiles.
metrics.definition: Completed profiles divided by initiated profiles.
metrics.interpretation: Describes operational completion only.
limitations: Completion does not indicate validity or quality.

metrics.name: Time to Review
metrics.purpose: Measure elapsed review time.
metrics.definition: Review completion timestamp minus review start timestamp.
metrics.interpretation: Must be evaluated relative to review quality and consequence.
limitations: Faster is not always better.

metrics.name: Evidence Acquisition Burden
metrics.purpose: Track the burden required to construct richer profiles.
metrics.definition: Structured record of subject time, evaluator time, computational cost, tool requirements, accessibility burden, and privacy burden.
metrics.interpretation: Richer profiles must justify their additional burden.
limitations: Components may not be reducible to a defensible single number.

metrics.name: Decision Deferral Rate
metrics.purpose: Measure frequency of deferred decisions where evidence is insufficient.
metrics.definition: Deferred decisions divided by decision opportunities.
metrics.interpretation: Must be paired with error reduction, fairness, and harm avoidance.
limitations: Not currently authorized for high-stakes deployment.

principles: A model of a person is not the person.
Do not convert multidimensional observations into hidden universal rankings.
Treat uncertainty as a legitimate result.
Permit deprecation and rejection of failed dimensions or adapters.
prohibited_uses: persistent cognitive tracking without legitimate governance

consent.description: Real-person assessment should use an appropriate consent and awareness process for the context.

privacy.description: Multidimensional cognitive and behavioral profiles may be sensitive and should follow data-minimization and appropriate governance practices.

contestability.description: Consequential human-facing profiles require mechanisms for evidence inspection, correction, contextual supplementation, and review.

temporal_limits.description: Profiles represent observations under particular conditions and should not be treated as timeless identity claims.

accessibility.description: Accessibility conditions should be distinguished from construct-relevant constraints where possible.
requirements: avoid treating irrelevant barriers as capability by default

fairness.description: Fairness analysis should examine errors, uncertainty, evidence coverage, mismatch, abstention, escalation, and downstream effects.

human_review.description: Qualified human review is required before consequential interpretation unless a specific use has separately achieved appropriate validation and governance.

misuse_boundary: Do not equate profile shape with identity.
Do not infer global intelligence from incomplete profile coverage.
Do not treat unusual profile topology as automatic superiority.
Do not treat substrate effects as automatic evidence of hidden ability.
Do not treat TriadicFrameworks adapters as validated merely because they are canon-aligned.
Do not use richer measurement as richer surveillance.
known_limits: No complete theory of intelligence is established.
RIQF dimensions are not validated psychological constructs.
Cross-species and cross-system equivalence is not established.
The module is not validated for consequential decision-making.
